extracted.intended_audience: DOE communications staff, press officers, technical writers, and authors of DOE press releases, reports, and outreach materials
extracted.subtask_description: A departmental style guide for writing and formatting DOE communications (press releases, reports, web copy, and technical publications), covering grammar, punctuation, capitalization, units, figures, dates, and domain-specific terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: en dash for ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an en dash (not an em dash or hyphen) to indicate ranges or to substitute for the word "to." Do not use en dashes to mean "and."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 25–45 cm2; 2–5 runs per hour; See sections 3.1–3.6; Jan. 16–Feb. 3, 2011; pages 1–5. In date spans, do not use "from" with an en dash — use either "from Jan. 16 to Feb. 3" or "Jan. 16–Feb. 3." For "between" use "and" (e.g., "between 25 and 30" not "between 25–30").

rubrics_metrics.name: data, datum, dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: "Data" is the plural of "datum." Use singular verbs/pronouns for data in general-audience and data-journalism contexts; in scientific/academic writing prefer plural verbs/pronouns. "Dataset" is one word and refers to a collection of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific: "Assorted data were collected." General audiences: "The data is sound." Examples: "A datum escaped his count." "The dataset includes all measurements."

rubrics_metrics.name: data in tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Place a zero to the left of the decimal in any number less than 1 in text and tables; align columns of numerals vertically on the decimals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If units of measurement differ in a column, alignment is not necessary but units must be specified. Examples: 0.5, 0.039. Ensure decimals align and units are clearly indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: dates (formatting and ranges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use month, numeral, year in American order (month day, year) for announcements and publicity. Abbreviate certain months when used with a specific date, spell out months when used alone or with a year only, and set off the year with commas when month, day, and year are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviate Jan., Feb., Aug., Sept., Oct., Nov., Dec. when used with a specific date. Examples: Sept. 20, 2021; Jan. 1–5, 2019 (use en dash for ranges, no spaces). Do not use ordinal numbers except in prepared remarks/speeches. When listing only month and year, omit commas (e.g., "September 2020"). Decades: no apostrophes unless preceded by "the" (a woman in her 50s; the '90s). If days of week are included with a date range, consider separating them from the date range: "Monday through Thursday, Jan. 1–5, 2023."

rubrics_metrics.name: decision maker vs decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Write "decision maker" as two words; hyphenate "decision-making" when used as a compound modifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP Note: AP Style hyphenates both decision-maker and decision-making. Example: "The PUC acts as the decision maker on the issue."

rubrics_metrics.name: degree symbol and kelvin usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the degree symbol (º) next to the temperature scale symbol with no space; repeat the degree symbol in ranges. Express kelvins as K (no degree sign) and leave a space before the K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 36ºC; 85ºF; 32º–36ºC; 85 K. Use º for Celsius/Fahrenheit but K for kelvins (not ºK).

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Energy first-reference usage
rubrics_metrics.description: On first reference in press communications, use "Energy Department" as an acceptable shorthand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "Today, the Energy Department announced..." See U.S. Department of Energy for formal references. "Energy Department" may be used in headlines and press copy on first reference only.

rubrics_metrics.name: desalination (term definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define desalination as the process of removing salt from seawater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage example: "NLR scientists are actively researching desalination capabilities..." (term definition for consistency in communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: disclaimer requirement for CMEI publications
rubrics_metrics.description: CMEI publications must include a disclaimer; the specific disclaimer depends on the publication type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See CMEI-Branded Publications Developed by Third Parties for which disclaimer to use. (Instructional/procedural requirement for publication prep.)

rubrics_metrics.name: dish/engine systems styling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a slash (/) rather than a hyphen in the term dish/engine systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "The dish/engine system is a concentrating solar power (CSP) technology..." Use slash to separate the two major parts: the solar concentrator and the power conversion unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: dollars formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Express thousands with commas; express millions, billions, trillions in decimal form followed by the word (acceptable to use 'M' or 'B' in headlines); for costs less than $1 use a dollar sign in technical reports and papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: $5,000; $3 million budget; $1.2 billion; DOE Announces $3M in Funding (headline). $0.25 and $0.06 per kilowatt-hour. Do not use hyphens when the phrase is adjectival (Congress passed a $4.2 trillion budget).

rubrics_metrics.name: e.g. and i.e. punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Both e.g. and i.e. are always followed by a comma and are not italicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a semicolon before "i.e." or "e.g." and a comma after them when a clause (with subject and verb) follows. Examples: "..., e.g., nanotechnologies that..." "..., i.e., the production of branched C4–C7 hydrocarbons..."

rubrics_metrics.name: electric vehicle (EV) terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Define electric vehicle (EV) and its common variants; use the initialism EV on first reference if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "Electric vehicles, also known as plug-in electric vehicles..." Two basic types: all-electric vehicles (AEVs) and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellipses usage in quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ellipsis marks (three periods with a space on each side or the symbol) to indicate omissions in quotes; if omitted words follow a grammatically complete sentence, put a period then an ellipsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually avoid ellipses at the beginning or end of quotes; to add words, enclose them in brackets. For omitted full paragraphs, center three asterisks (* * *) between paragraphs. See also quotation marks guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: email and e-terms styling
rubrics_metrics.description: "Email" is acceptable without a hyphen; other e- terms use a hyphen (e-book, e-business, e-commerce).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "I sent an email to everyone." "e-book, e-business, e-commerce." Use hyphen for electronic-prefix terms except email.

rubrics_metrics.name: ENERGY STAR trademark use
rubrics_metrics.description: Always show ENERGY STAR in all capitals; include the registration mark (®) on first use except in headlines/headers where include ® in first use in the body instead. Do not repeat ® after first use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No space between ENERGY STAR and ®. Example headline: "What Is ENERGY STAR?" Body: "ENERGY STAR® is the government-backed symbol..."

rubrics_metrics.name: enhanced geothermal system (EGS) terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred term is enhanced geothermal system (EGS); may also be referred to as 'engineered geothermal system.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example descriptive usage: "A man-made enhanced geothermal system (EGS) can extract..." Provide acronym in parentheses on first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: equations and variable definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: All equation terminology must be defined and used consistently in text and in subsequent equations, figures, and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide variable definitions immediately following the equation. Example: dQ/dt = AK dT/dx where dQ/dt = time rate of heat transfer; A = area; K = thermal conductivity; dT/dx = thermal gradient.

rubrics_metrics.name: et al. usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use et al. (followed by a period) to indicate 'and others' in references; do not italicize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "Feynman, Hawking, Sagan, et al." Follow conventional reference formatting and punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: etc. usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using 'etc.' if possible. Do not add 'etc.' to the end of a list that already begins with 'for example' or 'e.g.' 'Etc.' always ends with a period and if it ends a sentence, it is preceded by a comma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "Letters, packages, etc., should go here." Prefer specific listing instead of etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: executive summary placement and length
rubrics_metrics.description: An executive summary should appear before the table of contents; it's usually unnecessary in short reports. It may be 5%–10% of the document and should stand independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include problem statement, background, concise analysis, main conclusions; number tables/figures within the executive summary as Table ES-1, Figure ES-1. See CMEI Communications Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: federal capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not capitalize 'federal' unless it is part of a formal name; capitalize when part of formal names to distinguish from other jurisdictional terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Federal Trade Commission (capitalized), federal government (lowercase when generic).

rubrics_metrics.name: figures formatting and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures include drawings, graphs, charts, schematics, photos; number figures sequentially, include a figure title (minimum), captions optional but desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In long reports include section/chapter numbers in figure numbers (Figure 1-1). In print use consistent line weight; computer-generated figures must be clear for reproduction. No period after an incomplete caption sentence; if full sentences follow, end captions with periods. Example: Figure 1. Renewables as a percent...

rubrics_metrics.name: fiscal year (FY) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out 'Fiscal Year' on first mention (e.g., Fiscal Year 2020); thereafter abbreviate as FY 2001. Always capitalize 'Fiscal Year' when referring to a specific year. On websites, spell out 'fiscal year.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviation FY## may be used in charts; the FY## format includes a space (FY 2001).

rubrics_metrics.name: footnotes and citation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use footnotes for explanatory or supplementary information; prefer placing explanations in text. If using footnotes for citations, include a complete citation (author, year, title, hyperlink at minimum) and ensure sources are searchable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use superscript numerals for footnotes; in table footnotes use superscript letters (a, b, c). The footnote number follows punctuation except it precedes a dash. For CMEI technical publications, follow the predominant citation style agreed with the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: fractions in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Use words instead of numerals for simple fractions in running text; use numerals with slashes for complex fractions and display built-up fractions centered vertically when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'a third of the way', 'one-fifth its actual size', 'three-fourths of the participants'. Complex: 1/64, 23/32, 5-1/2 days. Place a zero to the left of the decimal for fractions less than 1 (0.125).

rubrics_metrics.name: funding opportunities (NOFO) terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: As of FY2025 DOE has retired FOAs and is issuing NOFOs; the term 'Notice of funding opportunity' should not be capitalized unless an official name or title. Use plain language and avoid overusing the acronym NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct usage example for headline/body vs incorrect overusage of acronym: HEADLINE: Notice of Funding Opportunity: $3 Million Announced... Body text: ...announced a $3 million funding opportunity... Avoid: body text that repeatedly uses 'NOFO' unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: geofluid definition and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'geofluid' as any subsurface fluid (groundwater, geothermal fluids, basinal brines, petroleum, magmatic fluid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent term in technical descriptions; example sentence provided on humidified cycles using low-temperature geofluid water.

rubrics_metrics.name: geographic information system (GIS) capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not capitalize 'geographic information system' unless it's part of a proper noun; do not use 'geographical.' GIS is a well-known acronym and may be used on first reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'She developed a GIS database...'; prefer 'geographic' (not 'geographical').

rubrics_metrics.name: geographic regions capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize well-known regions of the United States when they appear by themselves (the East, the West, the South), but lowercase general area descriptions (the eastern United States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'the Southeast, the Pacific Northwest' (capitalized). 'southwestern Nebraska' (lowercase). Capitalize widely known geographic sections (Southern California).

rubrics_metrics.name: geopressured geothermal resource definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define geopressured geothermal resource as co-produced brine trapped under caprock with elevated pressures and typical temperatures 90°C to 200+°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use term accurately in technical communications; example sentence about an onsite geopressured-geothermal hybrid cycle plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: GETEM (Geothermal Electric Technology Evaluation Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: GETEM is an Excel-based tool built by Idaho National Laboratory to estimate Levelized Cost of Energy for definable geothermal scenarios and focuses on electrical power generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: GETEM does not assess direct-use geothermal or heat pumps. Use official tool naming and attribution when referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: geothermal heat pump (GHP) definition and COP
rubrics_metrics.description: Geothermal heat pump (GHP) is a ground-source or water-source heat pump using the earth's constant temperature; indicate efficiency by coefficient of performance (COP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define acronym on first use: Geothermal heat pumps (GHPs). Example explanation: COP = heat provided in Btu per Btu of energy input.

rubrics_metrics.name: gigawatt (GW) definition and first-use spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A gigawatt (GW) equals 1 billion watts, 1 million kilowatts, or 1,000 megawatts; spell out on first mention and give abbreviation thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'In the first nine months of 2019, the United States installed 7.1 GW of photovoltaic power.'

rubrics_metrics.name: glossaries and nomenclatures guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a report includes many symbols or technical terms, provide a glossary or nomenclature arranged alphabetically; group Greek letters separately. Nomenclatures usually go in the front; glossaries at the back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A less formal List of Terms may be used in place of a formal glossary/nomenclature. Use consistent styling and placement per document conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Google Earth and Google Maps attribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Google Earth/Maps images need attribution (e.g., ©2019 Google, Map Data ©2020 Tele Atlas); do not remove logos/attribution embedded in image content; if attribution doesn't fit in print, put separate adjacent attribution text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In video, attribution must appear on-screen for the duration the image is shown; altering Google Earth images is only legal if alterations are made by Google Earth software and correct attribution is included. Derivative works are prohibited (e.g., combining static map images). See Google Earth Permissions for latest guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: government lowercase
rubrics_metrics.description: Never capitalize 'government' unless it is the first word of a sentence or part of a formal name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'the federal government', 'a state government', 'the U.S. government'.

rubrics_metrics.name: heat mining (term usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'heat mining' conceptually as harvesting planet's geothermal resources; use as an analogical description when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term to describe potential future technologies, with contextual caution about speculative nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) styling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'hybrid electric vehicle' as three words with no hyphens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) combine the benefits of gasoline engines and electric motors.' Define acronym on first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: hyphens general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No hyphen is needed between many prefixes/suffixes and root words unless the root is a proper noun; use hyphens for clarity or to prevent confusion and between prefixes and proper nouns or dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: non-CMEI, mid-1990s, trans-American, pre-Civil War. Use two hyphens when adding a prefix to a word that already has a prefix (non-self-limiting). Omit hyphens for common unit modifiers that aren't ambiguous (high school students). Use hyphens with numbers in modifiers (2-ft.-diameter pipes) or rewrite to avoid them. Use hyphen if prefix ends in a vowel and next word starts with same vowel (co-op, intra-arterial) with listed exceptions (cooperate).

rubrics_metrics.name: intermittent vs variable (wind energy wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'intermittent' when describing wind energy; use 'variable' because 'intermittent' implies binary on/off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct: 'The power grid was experiencing intermittent outages.' Incorrect: 'Intermittent wind caused insufficient power generation.' Use 'variable wind' to describe wind behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: internet lowercase
rubrics_metrics.description: Lowercase 'internet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The story was all over the internet.'

rubrics_metrics.name: inverter definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define inverter as a device that converts DC to AC for stand-alone systems or to supply power to a grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'DOE has funded R&D for smart-grid ready inverters...' Use definition for clarity in communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: italics usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use italics sparingly for emphasis and for foreign words/phrases; italicize hyphenated prefixes to chemical formulas and titles of long-form documents, books, journals, newspapers, magazines, and taxonomic names (genus/species).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not italicize commonly used foreign terms in the field. Examples: in situ, in vivo, cis-, trans-. Book/journal titles italicized; article titles in quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: it's vs its
rubrics_metrics.description: Use "it's" as contraction for "it is" and "its" as the possessive; possessive its never uses an apostrophe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "It's a shame that the company lost its biggest investor."

rubrics_metrics.name: Kalina cycle capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Always capitalize 'Kalina' (after Dr. Alexander Kalina) when referring to the Kalina cycle thermodynamic process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The Kalina cycle uses a solution of two fluids with different boiling points...' Proper noun capitalization is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: kelvin unit styling (kelvin, K)
rubrics_metrics.description: When referring to the Kelvin scale, use capital K; when spelling out the unit use lowercase 'kelvin'. Express kelvins as K with no degree sign and leave a space before the K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The kelvin is the fundamental unit...' 'Higher kelvin temperatures (3600–5500 K)...' Use 'K' for symbol, not ºK.

rubrics_metrics.name: kilowatt (kW) and kilowatt-hour (kWh) first-use
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out 'kilowatt' on first mention and abbreviate as kW thereafter; similarly spell out 'kilowatt-hour' on first mention and abbreviate as kWh thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'An electric heater consuming 1000 watts (1 kilowatt) and operating for one hour uses one kWh.' If the unit is used only once, the initialism need not be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: laboratory and lab capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize 'Laboratory' or 'Lab' when used with a laboratory's proper name or when referencing accredited U.S. National Labs (per DOE style); lowercase in other contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) is a U.S. Department of Energy National Laboratory. The lab is known for its R&D...' Exceptions may be made per Front Office preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: life cycle spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Write 'life cycle' as two words and never hyphenate, even as an adjective, per AP style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'life cycle studies' (not life-cycle).

rubrics_metrics.name: light bulb spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'light bulb' as two words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A-type lamps are considered the classic type of light bulb used for general-purpose lighting.'

rubrics_metrics.name: lists (formatting and punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use numbered lists for ordered content or bulleted lists otherwise. Listed items should be parallel in construction. Capitalize first word after each number and end each item with terminal punctuation except for short noun-phrase items, where only final item is punctuated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer AP Style punctuation rules with a CMEI exception: short phrases or single-word lists omit end punctuation except for the final item. Do not use commas or semicolons at ends of listed items. Use numbered/lettered lists when items will be referenced elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: lithology (term definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define lithology as the study of rocks, particularly the character of a rock formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent term in geoscience communications; example sentence provided about granitic composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: low-e styling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use lowercase 'low-e' (abbreviation for low-emissivity) unless it begins a sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'low-e windows reflect infrared heat back into the home.' Use as adjective term consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing USA® naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the trademarked name Manufacturing USA® with the registered mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe Manufacturing USA® as comprising 14 national manufacturing institutes, public-private partnerships, etc., and include ® on first use as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: mathematical symbols spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave a space on either side of mathematical operation symbols (minus, plus, times), but not for the slash a/b (division). Leave a space between numerals and symbols of measurement such as cm and Å.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not leave a space between numerals and degree, dollar, or percent symbols (e.g., 32º, $100, 17%). Example formatting: T_in - T_amb ºC × 1.8, 24 cm, 1.058 Å. Do not leave space around > or < unless they are operation signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: megawatt (MW) first-use and abbreviation
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out 'megawatt' on first mention and abbreviate as MW thereafter; if megawatts used only once, the initialism need not be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The global sales of electrolyzers in 2017 were estimated to be 100 megawatts (MW) per year.'

rubrics_metrics.name: megawatt-hour (MWh) spelling and abbreviation
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out 'megawatt-hour' on first mention and abbreviate as MWh thereafter; a MWh equals 1,000 kWh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Shepherds Flat is expected to generate 1,800,000 megawatt-hours (MWh) of energy each year.'

rubrics_metrics.name: memoranda plural
rubrics_metrics.description: The plural of 'memorandum' can be 'memoranda' or 'memorandums.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either plural accepted; use consistently. Example: 'The White House issued several memoranda on the topic.'

rubrics_metrics.name: metric conversions guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide links/resources for quick online conversions of English units to metric units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested tools: Digital Dutch Unit Converter, Internet French Property Measuring Units Converter Table. Use SI prefixes for multiples where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: metric (SI) system shorthand
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'metric system' as shorthand for the SI (International System of Units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See SI (Metric) System guidance for formal unit usage and conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: microgrid definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define microgrid as a local energy grid with control capability that can disconnect from the traditional grid and operate autonomously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight uses such as demand response and time-of-use pricing. Spell as one word.

rubrics_metrics.name: microseismic events spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Write 'microseismic' as one word (no hyphen); microseism refers to faint earth tremor and 'microseismic event' for microearthquakes associated with industrial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use term consistently in seismology-related communications; example discussion of pore pressure and induced events.

rubrics_metrics.name: months and years (abbreviation and punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize months; abbreviate months with more than five letters when used with a specific date followed by a period; spell out months when used alone or with only a year; omit comma when month and year appear together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The workshop is scheduled for Jan. 9, 2020.' 'October 2018' (no comma). Abbreviate all months in tables but omit the period (Jan, Feb, Mar...). Use lowercase s (no apostrophe) for decade plurals (1990s).

rubrics_metrics.name: multijunction solar cell preferred term
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer the term 'multijunction (MJ) solar cell' over 'tandem solar cell.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define on first use and give acronym: 'multijunction (MJ) solar cell' and use consistently in technical communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiplication symbols consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Be consistent in choosing multiplication symbols (× or ·) or omit them using proximity/parentheses; if using × or ·, insert spaces before and after the symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When omitting symbol, use adjacency or parentheses (ab(cd)). If using symbol: a × b with spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: nation lowercase
rubrics_metrics.description: Always lowercase 'nation' when referring to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Our nation is a leader in renewable energy markets.' Use lowercase in general references.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Laboratory capitalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE style capitalizes 'Laboratory' or 'Lab' when used with a laboratory's full proper name or when referencing the DOE National Laboratories; lowercase other references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Oak Ridge National Laboratory unveiled Summit...' but 'the lab' for generic references. See laboratory and lab guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: nonattainment spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell 'nonattainment' as one word with no hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage in air-quality contexts: 'urban and nonattainment areas.'

rubrics_metrics.name: noncondensable gas definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A noncondensable gas is any gas that does not condense under pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in thermodynamic or power-plant descriptions; example: 'The steam, along with its noncondensable gases, is routed to the power plant...'

rubrics_metrics.name: numbers: units, time, and general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use numerals with units of measurement and time; spell out numbers less than 10 in outreach communications (not technical reports); use numerals to imply arithmetical values; align numbers by decimal in tables and put zero before decimal less than 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 2-1/2 hours, 4.5 months, 36 cm, 87 years, 25 kW. Spell out numbers less than 10 in outreach text: 'five-year plan.' When numbers begin a sentence, spell out. When related numbers include >9 and <10, use numerals for all (3, 12, and 18 trials). For precision, limit decimal places to two in textual materials unless special circumstances require more; consult experts before changing significant digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: numbers: punctuation, ranges, and scientific notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commas to separate groups of three digits in large numbers; use an en dash with no spaces for numeric ranges; express SI multiples with prefixes and powers of 10 where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 5,182; 113,728; ranges: 15%–25%, 6–12 cm, $3 million–$4 million. Scientific notation and SI prefixes for metric multiples (mm, MJ). Use 'between X and Y' rather than 'between X–Y.'

rubrics_metrics.name: fractions and decimals precision and display
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out simple fractions in text; use slash numerals for complex fractions and hyphenate mixed numbers; place a zero before decimals less than 1; limit decimalization to two places in text unless special circumstances require otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: one-fifth or 1/5; 2-1/2 cm or 2.5-cm-diameter solar cell; 0.96. For measurement uncertainties, express significant digits per discipline norms (e.g., ±0.2 nm).
